glosses: etwas ist Objekt von Mythen und Erzählungen
tags: Hilfsverb haben; bildlich; Sagen ranken sich um etwas

examples.text: Um König Ludwig II. ranken sich viele Geschichten. Er soll homosexuell gewesen sein, was natürlich damals für einen König unmöglich war.

glosses: To ascend; rise; to go up.

examples.text: Prices climbed steeply.
Black vapours climb aloft, and cloud the day.
So we continue climbing to the saddle of the Kleine Scheidegg, where ahead there comes into view the wide expanse of the Grindelwald valley, backed by the snowy crown of the Wetterhorn.

After Bridge of Orchy, the line climbs steeply into the wild country of Rannoch Moor. The railway builders chose a different route across the moor from the road - we are completely on our own up here.

glosses: To mount; to move upwards on.

examples.text: climbing a tree
They climbed the mountain.

Other Hooverian devices become familiar too. Characters often have names that are so obscure they barely seem like real names (Ryle, Lowen, Chastin, Atlas, Crew) but might wind up climbing the baby name list — now you know why — in a few years’ time.

glosses: To scale; to get to the top of something.

examples.text: He is a curly-haired schoolboy barely in his teens, but 13-year-old Jordan Romero from California has become the youngest person to climb Mount Everest.

glosses: To move (especially up and down something) by gripping with the hands and using the feet.

examples.text: My legs were so stiff and my arms so sore that this morning barely could climb out of bed.
A priest clad in a white robe climbs the tree and with a golden sickle cuts the mistletoe, which is caught in a white cloth.

She thought she must have been mistaken at first, for none of the scarecrows in Kansas ever wink; but presently the figure nodded its head to her in a friendly way. Then she climbed down from the fence and walked up to it, while Toto ran around the pole and barked.
Cutter and Bolan climbed around the furniture and piled into the back of the truck.

glosses: To practise the sport of climbing.
To jump high.

examples.text: The defender climbed majestically at the near post to convert Johnson's corner.
As the game moved towards injury time, the Ospreys forced a line-out which Jonathan Thomas climbed high to take.
Four minutes of stoppage time were virtually up when Ricketts climbed to head in the equaliser from substitute Nicky Southall's centre.

glosses: To move to a higher position on the social ladder.
To move to a higher position on a chart, table, society, etc.

examples.text: The hit song has climbed to the number one spot.

glosses: Of plants, to grow upwards by clinging to something.
An act of climbing.

examples.text: Make sure that you keep checking to see that everything remains safe throughout the climb.

glosses: The act of getting to somewhere more elevated.

examples.text: The Mur de Péguère is a savage little climb, its last four kilometres a narrow tunnel of trees and excited spectators urging on the straining riders.
I guess the room wasn't so bad, except for the climb to get there. The stairs were destined to be a serious health hazard.

glosses: An effort of moving upward.

examples.text: After a decade of prosperity, millions of Asians are likely to be pushed into poverty, and the climb out of poverty will stall for millions of others.
This memorial dedicated to those / Who persished on the climb
An extended climb in Treasury yields risks exacerbating the pressures that have dogged a broad array of assets in recent months.

glosses: To advance or increase with stealth, unnoticed (literally or figuratively).

examples.text: The lioness has to creep up behind her prey so as not to be noticed.
Then I was forced to rest; and, sitting down on the ground, saw that the glimmering streak of light had faded, and that the awful blackness of the previous night was creeping up again.
Her exploration of emotion, too, is slightly muted. You have to stop and consult yourself. Pain — or joy or passion — creep up afterwards. These poems never hit you over the head.
These days cramped classrooms are all too common, with class sizes creeping up.

glosses: Gravir, monter en s’agrippant.

examples.text: Nous gagnons le haut de la ville et suivons d'abord la route de la Perdoma ; puis, obliquant à gauche, nous nous engageons dans un chemin grimpant la montagne entre une double haie d’agaves couvertes de liserons et de géraniums arborescents.

Le fossile d'une espèce disparue de kangourous a révélé d'étonnantes capacités à grimper aux arbres, il y a environ 50 000 ans dans une plaine d'Australie, aujourd'hui… dépourvue d'arbres, selon une étude parue mercredi.
Grimper au haut d’un arbre, à une muraille.
Un chat qui grimpe à un arbre, le long d’un arbre.
Les perroquets aiment à grimper.

glosses: S’élever en s’accrochant aux corps voisins, en parlant de la tige d’une plante.

examples.text: Cette vigne a grimpé jusqu’au premier étage.

glosses: Monter avec peine.

examples.text: […]; des multitudes éperdues grimpèrent par d’effrayants sentiers jusqu’à ces régions si élevées que les arbres ne poussaient plus.

Où, ô Hugo, cherchera-t-on ton nom ?
Justice enfin faite que n’a-t-on ?
Quand donc au corps qu’Académie on nomme
Grimperas-tu, de roc en roc, rare homme ?
Moi je grimpe à ma chambre avec maman.

glosses: S’emballer, réagir vivement.

examples.text: – Tu vas trop loin, Thérèse, permets-moi de te le dire ; même en plaisantant et pour me faire grimper, tu ne dois pas toucher à la famille.

glosses: Action consistant à grimper.

examples.text: L’extrémité du petit trochanter se trouve en dehors de l’axe mécanique du membre, et cela est d’autant plus marqué que ces animaux abductent fréquemment la hanche, particulièrement au cours du grimper.
Vous êtes forts au grimper à la corde?... Il reste neuf secondes.
